name: Goatsnake
label: Southern Lord
lede: Sabbath-slow riffs from a Seattle guitarist, a rhythm section from The Obsessed and a hardcore vet who sings like soul music.

eras.title: Riffs from Seattle, rhythm from the Obsessed
eras.text: Greg Anderson moved from Seattle to Los Angeles with a stack of slow riffs and found a ready-made rhythm section from a broken-up doom legend. Add a hardcore-punk singer with a soul voice and the band had its odd, warm identity.

years.cap: The original lineup: Anderson, Stahl, Pinhas, Rogers
years.h: [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] moves to LA and starts Goatsnake
years.p: Anderson, from Seattle and [[Thorr's Hammer|31c2d9e6-5f45-4b4e-9af1-aa46bbe3d4f9]], teams with bassist Guy Pinhas and drummer Greg Rogers, late of [[The Obsessed|aa043c18-c0a0-4cbe-bda0-8541f1fe59bd]], plus singer Pete Stahl of [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] and [[Wool|ada7ccb0-8dd8-467c-9859-abb0683884bb]].
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band's formation to 1996 in Los Angeles. Anderson has said the rhythm section's Obsessed pedigree made writing for them intimidating at first, and that he was the band's main songwriter.

Stahl, best known as the singer of Washington DC hardcore band Scream, whose drummer was a teenage Dave Grohl, gave the heavy riffs a voice Anderson described to Vice as sweet and melodic, closer to soul than doom.

years.p: Goatsnake's first records are a pair of 1998 singles, IV on Prosthetic Records and Man of Light on Warpburner Records.

eras.title: Man's Ruin, Southern Lord and a quick goodbye
eras.text: Two albums and a stack of split releases in three years. The band toured Europe and shared stages with Queens of the Stone Age and Electric Wizard, then drifted apart with no formal breakup.

years.h: Goatsnake Vol. 1 arrives on Man's Ruin and Rise Above
years.p: The debut runs about 37 minutes and includes the short instrumental "Dog Catcher" and the six-minute-plus "What Love Remains", with Danny Frankel adding percussion.
years.xp: Some listings, including Riffipedia, call the album simply I. Wikipedia titles it Goatsnake Vol. 1. Ten years later Anderson said the band played every song from it at Roadburn except "Dog Catcher".

years.h: Guy Pinhas leaves; Stuart Dahlquist takes over bass
years.p: Wikipedia says Pinhas left to join Acid King and was replaced by Stuart Dahlquist of [[Burning Witch|e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a]].

years.h: Split album with Burning Witch on Hydra Head
years.p: Goatsnake shares a record with Anderson's other band Burning Witch, Dahlquist's old group, on Hydra Head Records.

years.h: Dog Days EP, a Free cover and a Southern Lord number
years.p: Southern Lord catalog SUNN05 collects "The Orphan", "Long Gone", "Raw Curtains", "Man of Light" and a cover of Free's "Heartbreaker".
years.xp: The material was recorded between 1997 and 1999. In 2004 Southern Lord repressed it on vinyl, limited to 500 copies, with a Black Sabbath cover added, and also combined it with the debut on one CD as 1 + Dog Days.

years.h: Flower of Disease, produced by Nick Raskulinecz
years.p: The second album, 44 minutes over eight songs, has Dahlquist on bass and Dave Catching on lap steel for "El Coyote".
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists a release date of October 31, 2000 on Southern Lord and Man's Ruin. AllMusic praised its mix of modern production, riffing and grooving ambience, and LA Weekly noted the band's blend of slickness and weirdness.

Southern Lord reissued the album years later; Anderson said the band gradually went inactive after it.

eras.title: Sleeping without splitting
eras.text: Goatsnake never announced an end. Anderson was busy with Sunn O))) and Southern Lord, and the band showed up only once in a decade.

years.h: Goatsnake returns with a new bassist and drummer for Trampled Under Hoof
years.p: Anderson and Stahl are joined by bassist Scott Reeder of Kyuss and The Obsessed and drummer JR Conners of Cave In for a Southern Lord EP.
years.xp: Anderson told The Obelisk the band went inactive again after the EP, with his commitments to Sunn O))) part of the reason.

eras.title: Roadburn calls
eras.text: A festival invitation turned a dormant band into a working one again, with the original lineup.

years.h: Roadburn organizers spot Anderson and Pinhas at Supersonic
years.p: At the Supersonic festival in Birmingham they saw Greg Anderson and Guy Pinhas together and asked whether Goatsnake might play again.

years.h: Original lineup headlines Roadburn's opening night
years.p: Anderson, Stahl, Pinhas and Rogers reunite in Tilburg, the Netherlands, for their first show together in about a decade.
years.xp: Anderson said that they remembered how much fun it was and kept playing select shows afterwards. Southern Lord reissued Flower of Disease around the same time, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Black Age Blues
eras.text: With the old lineup mostly intact, a new bassist and a first album in fifteen years.

years.h: No tribute act, just new songs
years.p: Anderson said the band did not want to become a tribute act, so it wrote a whole album rather than replaying the old ones.
years.xp: He told Vice the album was made so the band would keep going. It was written despite the limited time everyone had, with Anderson describing finding time as the band's central challenge.

years.h: Black Age Blues on Southern Lord, first album since 2000
years.p: Anderson, Stahl and Rogers are joined by bassist Scott Renner, with Nick Raskulinecz producing again.

years.cap: Goatsnake at Le Guess Who?, Utrecht
years.h: Goatsnake and Sunn O))) share Le Guess Who? 2015
years.p: Anderson played both bands at the festival, calling Goatsnake a completely different can of worms.
Both Goatsnake and Sunn O))) were confirmed for Hellfest in 2016; Riffipedia describes it as the band's last major show before quiet.
